frontier.hypothesis: The 2 residual instructions of the after-main arming loop (the decrement and the back branch of do { lim = 0xC8; } while (--i);) are the entire distance from a proven score-5 body to 0, and that loop is inadmissible only because it is dead -- a spelling in which those two instructions do semantically-required work would close the function.
frontier.mechanism: s11 proved the arming geometry is exhaustively two shapes (after-main, score 5; nested-inner, score 8) via the last-first scan order at tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:435. The after-main shape needs only: (i) a loop whose beginning follows the main loop's, (ii) non-phony at loop.c:570 (its first insn after LOOP_BEG must be a CODE_LABEL), (iii) a move of the SAME pseudo the main loop scans first (regno 75, the named 0xC8). Nothing else about it matters to loop.c.
frontier.next_probe: Search the function's own semantics for work that can legitimately be expressed as a second loop after the main loop. Specifically re-examine the two-pass formulation: because the shrink states (2 and 4) zero the state word and the grow states (1 and 3) advance it to 2 and 4, a pass over both entries handling only states 2 and 4, followed by a pass over both entries handling only states 1 and 3, appears order-equivalent to the single interleaved pass. Measure it, and read whether jump2 cross-jumps the two loop bodies back toward one. Read build_insns AND the .loop dump (the second loop must print moved for regno 75 and the main loop must print halved since already moved).

frontier.hypothesis: A construct other than a loop can set moved_once[75] before the main loop is scanned, arming the doubling with no emitted control code at all.
frontier.mechanism: moved_once[regno] = 1 is written at exactly one site, tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:1912, reached only from move_movables' move block; the doubling reads it at loop.c:1609. s8 killed do { } while (0) (phony at loop.c:570), s9 killed same-value matching (m->match entries are marked done and skipped by the guard at loop.c:1584), and s11 killed the arm-from-an-earlier-textual-loop shape by scan order.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:1636-1720 (the m->partial && m->match branch and the m->move_insn branch) for any path that reaches line 1912 without a second NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG -- specifically whether a partial movable (m->partial with a non-VOIDmode m->savemode) can be produced by a sub-word store to the same local that carries the 0xC8. Confirm with a .loop dump before spending a build.

frontier.hypothesis: The 13-point residual can be lowered without changing loop.c's decision at all, by changing which hard registers the four hoisted constants receive.
frontier.mechanism: The four constants are hoisted into $8/$9/$10/$11 while the target uses a reused $v0 in-loop. The engine score is a weighted metric in which register mismatches cost less than insn insert/delete, and the ledger has never measured whether the pre-header emission order of the four li insns changes their allocation. A lower gradient would give the next session a sharper signal even though the loop.c decision is unchanged.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_8007526C/dumps/text1b.greg for the allocation order of regnos 124/126/127/128, then permute the case-label order in the switch (1/3/2/4 as today, vs 1/2/3/4, vs 2/1/3/4) and measure score for each; the case order changes expand_case's emission order and hence the pre-header order of the four li insns.
